question: Catholic teaching uses John 20:22-23 to defend sacramental confession. What is the apologetic argument?

choices.A: Jesus breathes the Spirit on the apostles and grants them authority to forgive or retain sins — a real judicial power requiring knowledge of specific sins, not just a general announcement
choices.B: The verse only means that apostles can announce that God has forgiven someone's sins
choices.C: The passage applies only to the apostles personally, not to their successors
choices.D: Retaining sins in this context means remembering sins for future judgment, not priestly authority

teaching.title: John 20:22-23 and Sacramental Confession
teaching.body: In John 20:22-23, the risen Christ breathes on the apostles and says 'Whose sins you forgive are forgiven them, and whose sins you retain are retained.' The Catholic argument: (1) this is a real act of conferring authority, not merely proclaiming existing forgiveness; (2) to retain or forgive specific sins meaningfully, the minister must know those sins — hence auricular (verbal) confession; (3) this authority is passed to successors through Holy Orders. The Eastern Orthodox also accept sacramental confession on this basis. The verse is the primary NT warrant for the sacrament.
